label: KVP-3600, symptom 'component_thermal_damage'
headline: Power-stage thermal failures on KVP-3600 inverters are landing exclusively on the 2024-build cohort (179 of 376 units, ~61 labour hours and multiple IGBT/gate-driver swaps in seven weeks) while older builds show none — worth an OEM engineering review and warranty preservation now, not after next summer.
action: Open an OEM engineering review of the power stage and gate-driver thermal design on the 179 2024-build KVP-3600 units, request build records for weeks 19-34 of 2024, and file/preserve warranty claims for the IGBT module and gate-driver replacements in WO-2026-00480, WO-2026-00522, WO-2026-00696 and WO-2026-00702 before next cooling season.

label: KVP-3600 manufactured 24Q3 (44 units): hard_fault x5, component_thermal_damage x5, ground_fault x3, overtemperature_trip x3
headline: A 44-unit KVP-3600 24Q3 build is failing power stages from a repeatable cooling-then-IGBT-damage chain across both hot and coastal sites while still under parts warranty — file the cohort claim before the window closes.
action: Open a cohort-level warranty case with Kelvara covering all 44 KVP-3600 24Q3 units citing the repeated 'IGBT module 2 / busbar heat marked' signature and fan-control rev 4.2.1, and inspect the remaining ~29 un-ticketed cohort units for heat-marked busbars, pitted DC contactors and firmware revision.

label: KVP-3600, symptom 'hard_fault'
headline: Three of eight KVP-3600 inverters from a single 2024 week-32 build lot failed their IGBT power stage at three separate sites within 24 days, all OEM-authorised under warranty — pursue the remaining five units of that lot as a batch claim before coverage lapses.
action: Open a lot-level warranty case with Kelvara citing WO-2026-00626, WO-2026-00677 and WO-2026-00680, request the build records and IGBT/gate-driver lot traceability for the KVP36-2432C week-32 2024 block, and inspect or proactively schedule the five remaining units in that block while parts coverage is live.

label: Vireo Valley, symptom 'hard_fault'
headline: Vireo Valley's 3.6x hard-fault rate is not an inverter problem — five of eight events are MV collector cable and switchgear terminations across three blocks, including two cable faults at the same run position on different circuits, and the site's inverter fault rate is at fleet baseline once those are removed.
action: Commission VLF tan-delta and partial-discharge testing plus a termination/splice audit on the Vireo Valley MV collector circuits serving B01, B03 and B04 and the main feeder, and pull the EPC construction records for those pulls to establish whether the terminations fall under the original installation warranty.

label: Caprock Mesa: repeated cleaned_or_serviced on module with declining benefit
headline: Washing blocks B01 and B03 at Caprock Mesa now returns about 1-2% instead of the historical ~5%, with technicians confirming clean glass and re-washing to no effect — the remaining deficit is likely not soiling and warrants a module diagnostic before further wash spend on those blocks.
action: Commission a module-level diagnostic on B01 and B03 (IV-curve sampling plus EL or handheld IR on representative strings) paired with one controlled long-interval wash on B01 to separate irreversible optical/electrical loss from wash cadence, and fix the asset_id-versus-narrative mismatch in the wash work-order template before the next cycle.

label: Caprock Mesa: repeated part_replaced on module with declining benefit
headline: Twenty-five modules at Caprock Mesa have been broken across four separate mower rock-strike incidents because contractually specified mower deck deflectors were never fitted — a preventable, recurring loss with an open technician recommendation unactioned since September 2024.
action: Issue a vegetation-management corrective action requiring the mow contractor to fit the site-specified deck deflectors and evidence compliance before the next mow cycle, and close out the open recommendation from WO-2024-00175.

label: Coralito Flats, symptom 'comms_loss'
headline: Coralito Flats generates roughly 3.7x the fleet rate of comms-loss work orders, but every one closed with the asset producing normally and no MWh lost - this is an alarm-configuration and truck-roll problem worth about 30 labor hours over two years, not an equipment failure worth a campaign.
action: Apply a dwell/de-bounce timer and auto-clear rule to Coralito Flats comms alarms so self-restoring dropouts under a set duration log to the historian instead of dispatching a truck, and fold a one-pass daisy-chain and termination inspection of B01/B03/B05/B06 plus the surge protection at B07 into the next scheduled PM sweep.

label: Caprock Mesa, symptom 'ground_fault'
headline: Caprock Mesa's ground-fault rate looks elevated mainly because a common fleet-wide chafe/connector failure mode is being logged there in bursts, but four blocks have repeat faults with no fault found and softening insulation readings that merit a one-shift megger survey rather than a site-wide campaign.
action: At the next scheduled Caprock Mesa PM, run and record quantitative insulation-resistance readings on all strings in blocks B02, B04, B06 and B07 and trend them against the 'low side of normal' values noted in WO-2026-00598, and fix the asset-ID/block mismatch in WO-2026-00598 so recurrence can be tracked per block.

label: Dry Creek Junction, symptom 'drive_grease_degradation'
headline: Dry Creek Junction's 8.8x tracker-drive grease signal is an aging 2017 block being greased reactively and coded as corrective work — 8 drives, 27.6 labor hours, no lost generation — fix it with a PM route addition, not a warranty claim.
action: Add the remaining 2017-vintage tracker drives at Dry Creek Junction to the existing tracker-drive lubrication PM route (as WO-2025-00537 recommends) and have the CMMS owner confirm these lube events are booked as PM rather than CM so the site's corrective rate stops reading as an 8.8x outlier.

label: KVP-3600, symptom 'thermal_derate'
headline: Seven afternoon derate tickets on KVP-3600 inverters look like the units' own high-ambient protection working as designed — 6 of 376 units, self-recovering, no outages — so hold at monitoring until Kelvara confirms the derate setpoint against spec.
action: Consolidate the four open Kelvara cases (WO-2025-00688, WO-2025-00908, WO-2026-00571, WO-2026-00586) into a single vendor query for the KVP-3600 published derate curve and firmware thermal setpoint, and track afternoon derate MWh on the six named assets through the next hot season — re-open as a warranty claim only if derate is confirmed below the published ambient envelope or event count grows.

label: KVP-3600, symptom 'overtemperature_trip'
headline: Seven KVP-3600 overtemperature trips cleared by reset with zero parts and four confirmed repeats point to a fan-control firmware behaviour rather than hardware, but at 29.3 labor hours and ~3.5 MWh across two seasons this is a desk-level OEM question to fold into an existing warranty case, not a field campaign.
action: Attach the seven overtemp work orders to the already-open OEM thermal case from WO-2025-00908 and ask the vendor to confirm the current fan-control firmware baseline and whether fw 4.2.1 (seen on WO-2025-00847) is superseded, then pull firmware version during the next scheduled PM on the ~70 units in the 2024 wk18-35 band rather than dispatching for it.

label: KVP-3600 manufactured 24Q2 (53 units): hard_fault x5, corrosion_or_wear x5, cooling_airflow_low x5, thermal_derate x4
headline: The KVP-3600 24Q2 'defect cohort' does not survive comparison with matched controls — non-24Q2 units one build week apart show the same thermal derate, fan and ground-fault narratives, and the 2.57x lift is driven by repeat tickets on ~18 distinct assets rather than a build-specific failure.
action: Do not open a 24Q2 warranty action; instead re-cut the thermal chain (cooling_airflow_low, thermal_derate, overtemperature_trip, component_thermal_damage) across all KVP-3600 build quarters on a per-unit-operating-year and distinct-asset basis, and only reopen if the late-fan-ramp signal survives that normalisation.

label: TECH-0231 logs tracker work per ROW (91%) vs fleet 51%
headline: TECH-0231's 91% row-level logging is a work-mix artifact - peers at the same sites log row-level on row-scoped jobs and zone-level on zone-scoped jobs - so no technician coaching or commercial action is warranted; fix the metric instead.
action: Retire or re-stratify the technician row-share KPI so it is computed only within single-row-scope tracker work orders, rather than against a mixed fleet denominator that includes zone- and block-scope jobs.

label: Sundowner Mesa, tracker_structure: 27 tickets in 8 weeks from 2025-03-15
headline: The 27-ticket March tracker spike at Sundowner Mesa is cleanup from one microburst already under an open property claim, not an emerging tracker defect, and the count is inflated by zone-level and templated duplicate tickets.
action: Close the burst as storm remediation under claim NRS-PL-2025-0417, and monitor Sundowner Mesa tracker_structure tickets for the next two quarters for wind-independent limit-switch-bracket or incomplete-stow reports, re-opening as an engineering assessment only if that mode recurs.

label: MG-3300 manufactured 17Q4 (18 units): failure_to_start x2, ground_fault x2, cooling_airflow_low x2, hard_fault x1
headline: The MG-3300 17Q4 'cohort' is an artifact of six repeat visits on two Kernwood assets — per-asset failure rate is at the fleet median and every failure mode also appears at other sites, so there is no warranty case here.
action: Close the MG-3300/17Q4 cohort as not a build defect, and instead hand the two adjacent combiner-box conductor faults (WO-2025-00671, WO-2026-00050) and the open cable-sag walkdown items to the Kernwood site lead as a local BOS inspection task.

label: KVP-3600, symptom 'ground_fault'
headline: KVP-3600 ground faults are running at the fleet norm (1.1x peer median) and the same chafed-home-run and pinched-connector findings appear on CES40 and SLT25 units at the same sites — this is a cable-management/site issue, not an inverter-model defect, and warrants no warranty or vendor action.
action: Close this model-level candidate and re-cut the ground-fault population by site, combiner ID and racking/install vintage across all inverter models before any campaign is scoped, and separately fix the resolution-code vs narrative disagreement seen in WO-2025-00158, WO-2024-00338 and WO-2025-01192.

label: Sundowner Mesa, symptom 'tracker_mechanical_damage'
headline: Sundowner Mesa's 23x tracker-damage rate is storm backlog from the 14 March microburst already under an open property claim, inflated further by duplicate zone-level tickets — no systemic tracker defect and no new spend warranted.
action: Confirm all 20 work orders are booked to property claim NRS-PL-2025-0417, collapse the duplicate zone-level tickets (WO-2025-00278/WO-2025-00293 and WO-2025-00258/WO-2025-00387) before any rate reporting, and set a 90-day watch item on repeat 'limit switch bracket bent' tickets rather than opening an engineering campaign.

label: CE-4000, symptom 'ground_fault'
headline: CE-4000 ground faults are running at the fleet norm, not above it — the chafed home runs show up on other inverter makes too, so this is a wiring-workmanship question to re-scope by site, not a CE-4000 problem.
action: Close this candidate as a model-attribution artifact and re-cut all ground-fault work orders by site and combiner-block ID across every inverter model, starting with Kettle Run and its CB-B03/B04/B06 blocks, before committing any inspection crew time.

label: MG-3300, symptom 'ground_fault'
headline: MG-3300 ground faults run at the fleet-wide rate (lift 1.05) and the same chafed-home-run findings appear on other inverter models at the same sites — no MG-3300 claim or campaign is warranted.
action: Close CAND-024 without a warranty or remediation campaign, and instead fold the two tech recommendations to inspect sibling home-run entries at CB-B04 and CB-B08 (WO-2024-00235, WO-2024-00084) into the existing routine cable-management PM scope.

label: Salt Fork Landing, symptom 'comms_loss'
headline: Salt Fork Landing's comms_loss rate is within normal variation for its small exposure base — the reset tickets look identical to comparable work at Coralito Flats, Two Rivers Crossing and Pine Hollow, so no commercial action is warranted.
action: Take no remediation action; set a watch on Salt Fork Landing comms_loss and tracker-zone repeat visits (TR-Z03 in particular) and re-test the rate after another 3-6 GW-months of exposure, and correct the parts/resolution-code mismatch on WO-2025-00895.

label: Birch Coulee, symptom 'comms_loss'
headline: Birch Coulee's comms_loss rate is not a real site defect once split by component and compared against other sites, though two block fiber runs there are running with no spare-pair redundancy and need scheduled permanent repair.
action: Close the finding as ordinary variation, but open work items to permanently repair the two spare-pair-patched fiber runs at Birch Coulee (B02, B08) and re-check the site rate after another 6-12 months of exposure.

label: KVP-2400 manufactured 16Q1 (22 units): ground_fault x4, grid_ride_through x1, hard_fault x1, cooling_airflow_low x1
headline: The KVP-2400 16Q1 'cohort' is noise, seven unrelated failures across 22 units, and the ground faults inside it are the same combiner-level conductor damage seen on other models at other sites, so no warranty or campaign action is warranted.
action: Close this cohort as ordinary variation and instead track DC ground faults by combiner block across all sites, since CB-level chafing/pinch findings recur at Dry Creek Junction, Sablewood Ridge and Two Rivers Crossing regardless of inverter model or build quarter.

label: CE-4000, symptom 'cooling_airflow_low'
headline: The CE-4000 cooling flag is a labelling artifact — three unrelated causes (seized fans, loaded filters, bird nests) totalling 63.2 labor hours across 12 jobs share one symptom code, and none of them individually exceeds the peer rate, so no warranty or campaign action is warranted.
action: Send this back to the extraction/codebook owner to split 'cooling_airflow_low' into distinct labels (fan_fault, filter_blocked, intake_obstruction) and correct the component field mis-coding on WO-2025-00785, WO-2025-01089 and WO-2026-00369, then re-run the model-vs-peer rate comparison on the fan-fault subset alone before any commercial action.

label: Red Clay Flats, symptom 'drive_grease_degradation'
headline: Red Clay Flats' 10x tracker-grease rate is an artifact of booking routine regreases as corrective work orders while other sites book identical jobs as PMs - no defect, no reported production loss, and the underlying wear is vintage-driven.
action: Fix the work-order coding by folding tracker-drive lubrication PMs into the same numerator/denominator as CM grease work, then re-run the site-symptom rate before any field action; separately hand the technicians' block-sweep regrease suggestion to the site PM planner.

label: Sundowner Mesa, symptom 'tracker_misalignment'
headline: Sundowner Mesa's 3.4x tracker-misalignment lift is a copy-paste narrative and mis-coding artifact layered on top of March 2025 microburst cleanup, not a tracker defect — no warranty or remediation exposure, but the site's work-order data quality is degrading fleet analytics.
action: Close this as non-systemic and instead route Sundowner Mesa's work-order records to data governance to stop narrative templating and fix resolution_code/parts mismatches (e.g. WO-2025-01179 coded PART-REPL with no parts, WO-2026-00073 coded NO-FAULT-FOUND yet 7.0 labor hours and outcome 'resolved', WO-2025-00240 coded RESET with 'tracker motor x4').

label: Almond Row: repeated reset_or_restart on central_inverter with declining benefit
headline: No efficacy decay at Almond Row — the pattern is one escalated work order across five different inverters with no measured benefit data, and matched work orders at four other sites show the same reset-and-resolve behaviour.
action: Close this candidate and instead pull the full 2025 fault and reset history plus firmware revision for the single unit KVP36-2419B-0371 to confirm or dismiss its stated second overtemperature recurrence.

label: Ashvale Dry Lake, symptom 'drive_grease_degradation'
headline: Ashvale's 9x drive-grease rate is an artifact of one technician's templated write-ups and inconsistent resolution coding — the same failure appears at four other sites and should be investigated as a drive-vintage cohort, not an Ashvale problem.
action: Re-cut this analysis by tracker drive vintage/serial cohort across all sites rather than by site, and correct Ashvale's symptom and resolution coding (author-templated narratives and resolution_code/action mismatches) before any site-level rate is used again.

label: MG-3300, symptom 'grid_ride_through'
headline: The MG-3300 'grid ride-through' spike is a ticketing and symptom-labelling artifact — all 8 events self-cleared with no repair and peer inverters at the same sites show the same disturbances under a different label; ~32 technician hours over 21 months, no fleet exposure.
action: Reconcile the CMMS symptom taxonomy so self-clearing ride-through alarms are logged as informational events rather than CM work orders (and are not split from 'undervoltage_trip'), then re-run the model×symptom screen on alarm counts rather than WO counts.

label: KVP-3600, symptom 'corrosion_or_wear'
headline: KVP-3600 cooling-fan replacements are running at roughly 2% of units per year with no alarms, no repeats and comparable fan failures on older builds recorded under other labels — this is consumable wear, not a warranty or defect case.
action: Close the candidate and instead add a standing metric of fan replacements per unit-year by build quarter across all symptom labels (text-matched on 'fan' + 'bearing'), revisiting only if the 2024-build cohort exceeds the older-cohort rate by a clear margin.

label: Blackfoot Draw: repeated repaired_in_place on conductor_or_connector with declining benefit
headline: Blackfoot Draw's 'declining repair effectiveness' is a tagging artifact — three unrelated failure modes merged under one component label with zero recorded benefit data — and the only real item inside it is a routine clip upgrade on three blocks that belongs in the next mow-cycle cable pass.
action: Split the 'conductor_or_connector' tag into termination/connector vs cable-support before re-running the efficacy detector, and confirm whether the recurrence flag on WO-2026-00564 is linked to a prior WO ID or only inferred from free text; separately, add the heavier north-block clip to the next scheduled mow-cycle cable pass on B02/B03/B04 as routine work, not as an escalation.

label: Vireo Valley: repeated cleaned_or_serviced on module with declining benefit
headline: The Vireo Valley 'wash benefit collapsing from 8% to 2%' signal is two hand-typed estimates on two different blocks with templated narratives and miscoded resolution codes — no action warranted beyond fixing how wash outcomes are recorded.
action: Close this candidate and instead require wash work orders at Vireo Valley to record pre/post soiling-ratio or SCADA-derived MWh with the correct CLEANED resolution code, so wash efficacy can be tested on real repeat-block data next season.
